candidates.label: Al-Maghtas / Wadi al-Kharrar (Jordan, east bank)
candidates.support: Byzantine-period churches, hermit caves and baptismal structures excavated on the Jordanian east bank match the site's depiction on the sixth-century Madaba mosaic map, making it the most archaeologically supported candidate; this is the basis of its UNESCO World Heritage listing as the traditional site of John's baptisms.

candidates.label: Qasr al-Yahud (West Bank, opposite bank)
candidates.support: A parallel pilgrimage site on the river's west bank with two fifth-century Byzantine churches; excavation and survey reports for this side of the river have not documented occupation layers as early as the first century, making it, on present evidence, a weaker archaeological candidate than Al-Maghtas for the Gospel event itself.

summary.text: Bethany beyond the Jordan, named in John 1:28 as the place where John the Baptist was baptizing, including Jesus, is located east of the Jordan River; its precise site is debated, and the wording itself was altered to 'Bethabara' in some later manuscripts and older English translations.

history.text: The third-century scholar Origen could not find a village called Bethany east of the Jordan in his own day and proposed emending the text to 'Bethabara' ('house of the ford'), a reading that entered later manuscripts and older English translations, though the earliest and best-attested Greek manuscripts read 'Bethany.'

Some scholars have proposed a location farther north and east, in the region historically called Batanea, as a better fit for the Gospel's geography and for John the Baptist's later arrest by Herod Antipas; this remains a minority academic view without a single agreed coordinate.

scripture.textWEB: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
